name: Harbin Mahjong
description: Harbin Mahjong is a regional Mahjong variant associated with Harbin and wider northeast China play. It follows the standard Mahjong draw-discard loop with meld claims and a complete-hand win condition, while using local table conventions for what hands qualify and how points are assessed.

history.origins: Harbin Mahjong reflects regional Mahjong table practices in northeast China, evolving from shared Mahjong foundations into a recognizable local rules profile.
timeline: 20th century: regional rules propagate through social play.
Modern era: common profiles are recorded and implemented in digital rulesets.
history.cultural: It is played socially in homes and community settings, often with agreed table profiles before play begins.
history.evolution: Core hand structure remains aligned with Mahjong, while local preferences influence the scoring profile and what wins are considered valid.

setup.deck: Standard Mahjong set with suited tiles, honor tiles, and bonus tiles according to table profile.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 tiles; dealer receives 14 and discards first.

rules.objective: Complete a legal winning hand that satisfies the active Harbin scoring profile.
rules.gameplay: On each turn, a player draws from the wall and discards one tile. Other players may claim a discard for a legal meld under claim priority. A player wins when their concealed plus melded tiles form a complete hand and the profile's validity requirements are satisfied.
keyRules: Draw then discard is the default turn sequence.
Claim legality governs when discards can be taken for melds.
A valid win requires a complete 14-tile hand and accepted scoring validity.

strategy.basic: Build efficient hand shapes and prefer waits that keep multiple outs alive.
strategy.intermediate: Use visible tiles to estimate safety and avoid feeding likely completes.
strategy.advanced: Balance speed, defense, and value with profile-aware scoring routes and opponent tempo.
tips: When behind, prioritize completion speed over rare high-value patterns.
When an opponent's melds indicate a single suit, treat that suit's key tiles as higher risk discards.
